summary: Unexpected duplicate credit/usage apportionment after subaccount split leading to invoice delta
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports an unexpected increase on their finalized invoice following a planned subaccount split last week. The invoice shows the parent account and new subaccount both receiving applied buffer credits and embedded usage lines for the same job window.

Impact:
- Customer KiteHealth sees a ~13% higher charge for the billing period after the split.
- Discrepancy blocks autopay for this cycle until reconciled.

Environment:
- Production (us-west-2), Dedicated plan, embed-multilingual-v1 heavy batch runs (nightly microbatches).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Created subaccount "kite-research" on 2026-02-10 and initiated migration of hourly jobs.
2) Ran scheduled batch embedding job 2026-02-11 02:00-04:00 PST (microbatches).
3) Finalized invoice generated 2026-02-15 shows duplicate credit lines and duplicated embed usage lines for the same job IDs.

Logs / Evidence attached by customer in email:
- CSV of invoice line items (line IDs redacted)
- Example postback payloads for two job runs showing identical job_id and different tenant tags
- Screenshot of usage dashboard with parent+subaccount totals

Requested outcome:
- Clear explanation of why credits and usage were apportioned to both parent and subaccount.
- Correction or provisional credit applied before autopay runs.
- Recommendations to avoid recurrence during future subaccount splits.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: postback replay/deduplication failed during subaccount split migration, causing the same job postback to be attributed to both old and new tenant IDs.

Observed two postbacks in ingestion logs for same job_id with different tenant_tag values arriving within 3 seconds of each other. The reconciler currently uses 'tenant_tag' + 'job_id' as dedup key. Split process creates new tenant_tag while re-emitting historical postbacks for continuity leading to duplicate dedup keys mismatch.

Reproducer created in staging by simulating subaccount split: confirmed reconciler stored two separate meter events from identical payloads when tenant_tag changed mid-window. Aggregation step later applies buffer credit per meter event, leading to duplicate credits and usage lines on invoice.

Edge case: if split occurs while microbatch job is still in flight, the in-flight postbacks may be replayed with both tenant tags. Race between migration job that re-tags historical postbacks and live postbacks triggers duplication.
Workaround considered: temporary hold on re-tagging historical postbacks for a 10-minute window around active microbatch schedules; or use stable dedup key anchored to job_id + originating-key-hash.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing-reconciler/pull/512 implements job_id-first dedup key and ignores tenant re-tag events if original postback hash matches existing event.
Billing impact estimate: duplicated embed lines total $1,842. Customer saw a 13% uplift for the period. Provisional credit proposed for that amount pending final reconciliation.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation and resolution plan:
1) Applied provisional credit for duplicated lines (provisional-CR-291736) on 2026-02-20 to unblock autopay.
2) Deployed reconciler dedup hotfix to production 2026-02-21 (PR 512).
3) After running a full reprocess for the affected hourly window, final invoice adjustment will be posted and communicated by 2026-02-25.
4) Postmortem action items: add split-window guardrails to migration tool, update runbook to recommend pausing active microbatch schedules during subaccount re-tagging, add unit tests for dedup behavior.
5) Customer follow-up: scheduled 2026-02-22 call with KiteHealth operations to run through new runbook and confirm migration steps.

Final billing outcome (to be updated): pending reprocess. If reprocess confirms duplication, the provisional credit will be converted to a permanent invoice correction and an additional apology credit will be offered for operational disruption.
